\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آب} \fa{دادن} (âb dâdan)}{آب دادن (âb dâdan)}]{\fa{آب} \fa{دادن} (âb dâdan) — to water (plants)}

\label{lesson:FA-C222-ab-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to joke, then the Persian for to be jealous.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آب} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{آب} \fa{دادن}} — \emph{âb dâdan} — \textquotedblleft{}to water (plants)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âb dâdan} is \textquotedblleft{}to give water\textquotedblright{}: \emph{âb} is inherited (Middle Persian \emph{āb}, EtymDB). \emph{dâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*deh\textsubscript{3}-}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پارس} \fa{کردن} (pârs kardan)}{پارس کردن (pârs kardan)}]{\fa{پارس} \fa{کردن} (pârs kardan) — to bark}

\label{lesson:FA-C222-pars-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be jealous, then the Persian for to water.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پارس} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پارس} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{pârs kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to bark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pârs kardan} pairs \emph{pârs}, \textquotedblleft{}barking\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan}. Where \emph{pârs} comes from is not settled; it is not the name \emph{Pârs}, \textquotedblleft{}Persia\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB lists beside it. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خواب} \fa{دیدن} (khâb didan)}{خواب دیدن (khâb didan)}]{\fa{خواب} \fa{دیدن} (khâb didan) — to dream}

\label{lesson:FA-C222-khab-didan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to water, then the Persian for to bark.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خواب} \fa{دیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{خواب} \fa{دیدن}} — \emph{khâb didan} — \textquotedblleft{}to dream\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâb didan} is \textquotedblleft{}to see sleep\textquotedblright{}: \emph{khâb}, \textquotedblleft{}sleep\textquotedblright{}, is inherited (Middle Persian \emph{xwāb}, EtymDB), and so is \emph{didan}, \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB takes \emph{khâb} back to the Indo-European root \emph{*swep-}, \textquotedblleft{}to sleep\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طول} \fa{کشیدن} (tul keshidan)}{طول کشیدن (tul keshidan)}]{\fa{طول} \fa{کشیدن} (tul keshidan) — to take (time), to last}

\label{lesson:FA-C222-tul-keshidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to dream, then the Persian for to doubt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طول} \fa{کشیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{طول} \fa{کشیدن}} — \emph{tul keshidan} — \textquotedblleft{}to take (time), to last\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tul keshidan} is \textquotedblleft{}to draw out length\textquotedblright{}: \emph{tul}, \textquotedblleft{}length\textquotedblright{}, is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭūl} (root \emph{ṭ-w-l}, Lane), and \emph{keshidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to draw\textquotedblright{}, is native. \emph{keshidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to pull\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{kašīdan}.
\end{cousinweb}
